sources.title: Karl Otto Forster, Lectures on Riemann Surfaces (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 81, Springer, translated by Bruce Gilligan)
sources.locator: Chapter 2, §§12–18, printed pp. 96–153; exercises of §16, printed p. 131

contents.name: Ch. 1 §§1, 9-10: Riemann surfaces, differential forms and their integration; the definition of the order of a meromorphic function and differential
Ch. 2 §12.1-12.5: Cech cochains, cocycles, coboundaries, fixed-cover H^1, refinements and the direct limit H^1(X,F)
Ch. 2 §12.6: H^1 of the differentiable-function sheaf vanishes by a partition of unity (Forster uses direct-limit Cech cohomology)
contents.proof_mapping: Forster proves the first-cohomology case by splitting a Cech 1-cocycle. The registered prerequisite proves the stronger derived-sheaf-cohomology acyclicity for every smooth-function module sheaf and every positive degree; its proof uses exactness of global sections plus module-injective resolutions.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §12.8 (Leray): a cover with H^1(U_i,F)=0 computes H^1(X,F)
contents.proof_mapping: Supplies the acyclicity-to-comparison step identifying the finite good cover groups with sheaf cohomology.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §13.1-13.2: the local Dolbeault lemma, solving df/dzbar=g on a disc
contents.proof_mapping: The surjectivity on stalks of the dbar-resolution; the library's polydisc version is the cited supplier.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §13.4-13.5: H^1(disc,O)=0 and H^1(P^1,O)=0
contents.proof_mapping: Acyclicity of discs for the structure sheaf and of every finite good cover; the P^1 case is not used.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §§14.9-14.11, printed pp. 115-116: finite-dimensionality of H^1(X,O) on compact X and the genus convention; this source addresses the structure sheaf only.
contents.proof_mapping: Read as a scalar corroboration and alternate route only. The item proof uses the line-bundle Dolbeault Hodge theorem; this source does not establish finiteness for arbitrary O(D).

contents.name: Ch. 2 §14.9-14.11: restriction images of H^1(-,O) on a Riemann surface are finite-dimensional; dim H^1(X,O)<infinity on compact X; the definition g:=dim H^1(X,O)
contents.proof_mapping: Confirms the compact structure-sheaf case and genus convention; it is not the proof of arbitrary line-bundle finiteness used in this item.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §14.12-14.13: existence of a meromorphic function with a single pole in a relatively compact domain and interpolation at finitely many points
contents.proof_mapping: An alternative route to the existence statement; the page proves the same conclusion from Riemann-Roch instead. RR now supplies nonzero meromorphic-differential existence unconditionally; the canonical correction vanishes at every genus because deg(K−2g[p])=−2, with the genus-zero nonconstant function still obtained from [p].

contents.name: Ch. 2 §15.9(a),(c),(d) and §15.12-15.14: the short exact sequences 0->O->E->E^{0,1}->0, 0->C->O->Omega->0, the long exact sequence and Dolbeault's theorem H^1(X,O)=E^{0,1}(X)/dbar E(X)
Ch. 2 §§15.9(c), 15.12–15.15, printed pp. 123–126: the holomorphic de Rham sequence and de Rham cohomology on a Riemann surface
contents.proof_mapping: Independent corroboration of the de Rham and holomorphic de Rham passages. This item proves the constant-sheaf comparison directly from the local Poincare lemma and acyclic smooth-form modules.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §16.1-16.4: divisors, orders, degree, principal divisors and the sheaves O_D
Ch. 2 §16.4: the sheaves O_D as meromorphic functions that are multiples of -D, with O_{D+(f)} isomorphic to O_D
Ch. 16 §§16.6-16.9, printed pp. 128-130: the skyscraper sheaf, exact sequence with Laurent coefficient c_{-D(P)-1}, its cohomology sequence, and the Euler-characteristic increment for arbitrary D.
contents.proof_mapping: The coefficient formula and six-term sequence are checked directly in the item. The local coefficient is a polar term only for D(P)≥0; the item treats all integer D(P) and records the coordinate-dependent scalar identification.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §16.8-16.9: the surjection H^1(O_D)->H^1(O_{D'}) and the Riemann-Roch theorem dim H^0-dim H^1=1-g+deg D
contents.proof_mapping: The §16.7 exact sequence and §16.9 proof were read in full. Its base case uses h^0(O)=1 and h^1(O)=g, the point exact sequence gives the Euler increment, and the finite signed point decomposition handles every divisor. A10 supplies the topological-genus identification in this library. Focused local scope repair: intrinsic RR at D=−(g+2)[p] yields a nonzero section of K_X tensor O((g+2)[p]); division by the canonical meromorphic divisor-bundle section proves existence of a nonzero meromorphic differential and restores the unconditional canonical-divisor formula. This added argument is local supplier reasoning, not a new source-reading claim.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §16.11-16.13: existence of a meromorphic function with a pole of order at most g+1 and a covering X->P^1
contents.proof_mapping: The source applies Riemann-Roch to D=(g+1)[p], which yields a nonconstant function and a covering of degree at most g+1. This item preserves the designed exact value ell(2gp)=g+1 for g≥1 by deriving deg K at every genus from A10/A13/A15, and treats g=0 separately because a degree bound of 2g=0 is impossible. RR now supplies nonzero meromorphic-differential existence unconditionally; the canonical correction vanishes at every genus because deg(K−2g[p])=−2, with the genus-zero nonconstant function still obtained from [p].

contents.name: Ch. 2 §§17.1–17.3, printed pp. 132–134: the Dolbeault residue trace, Mittag-Leffler distributions with differences ωⱼ−ωᵢ, and Res(μ)=Res([δμ]) with its Stokes proof
Ch. 2 §§17.5–17.6, printed pp. 135–136: the residue pairing H⁰(X,Ω_{−D})×H¹(X,O_D) and Theorem 17.6’s local principal-part injectivity proof
Ch. 2 §§17.5–17.10, printed pp. 136–139: the residue-duality pairing, injectivity, Theorem 17.9 and the dimension consequence.
contents.proof_mapping: Forster’s Theorem 17.9 proves surjectivity using Riemann–Roch; this item derives duality from the earlier Hodge-star pairing and uses Forster as statement-level corroboration.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §17.12: the degree of a canonical divisor is 2g-2
contents.proof_mapping: The example obtains deg K=2g-2 from omega_C=L^{g-1} on the hyperelliptic curve; the general statement follows from Riemann-Roch and duality and is not needed as a separate item.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §17.14: the Riemann-Hurwitz formula
contents.reason: Riemann-Hurwitz is already published on the prerequisite CA-RS-1 page and is consumed there; this page does not re-derive it, so no local item is created for it.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §17.16: H^1(X,O_D)=0 for deg D>2g-2
contents.proof_mapping: Forster §§16.5,16.9–16.10,17.15–17.16 (printed pp. 128–130,141) and Looijenga Ch. 5 §2 (printed p. 52) and Ch. 6 (pp. 53–56) were read. Verification steps 1.1–2.1 use arbitrary-divisor section ratios, prove the degree-one criterion locally, and exclude common base points for the degree-two map; analytic hyperellipticity is stated explicitly and high-degree vanishing is proved through the local RR/duality chain.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §17.17-17.19: H^1(X,M)=0, globally generated sheaves O_D and the embedding theorem for deg D>=2g
contents.proof_mapping: The page proves the embedding by Riemann-Roch dimension counts for D, D-p-q and D-2p instead of by global generation theory.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §§18.1–18.2, printed pp. 151–152: obstruction class, solvability iff coboundary, and the residue criterion via Serre duality.
contents.proof_mapping: The proof uses Serre duality; this item derives the same criterion from the assigned A13 Hodge-derived duality, whose supplier remains escalated.

contents.name: Ch. 2 Exercises 16.1-16.3: Riemann-Roch on P^1 and on a torus; every disc cover is a Leray cover for O_D
contents.proof_mapping: Forster Exercises 16.1–16.2 (printed p. 131) and McMullen Ch. 9 (printed p. 85) were read in the full PDFs. Verification steps 1.1–3.1 prove the sphere dimensions and canonical divisor with H^0(K)=0, torus genus and dimensions, and the explicit Weierstrass distinct-pole-order basis; no Leray-cover claim is imported.

sources.title: Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Harvard Math 213b course notes (2026)

contents.name: Ch. 5-6: holomorphic and harmonic forms, the Hodge star and the Hodge norm on a compact surface
contents.proof_mapping: The metric, Hodge-star and L^2-pairing vocabulary supplied by the preceding Hodge-theory page is what the finiteness and residue-pairing items consume; the harvesting source is cited for that vocabulary.

contents.name: Ch. 8: the Dolbeault lemma on discs and the exact sequence 0->O->E^0->E^{0,1}->0, with H^1(X,O)=E^{0,1}(X)/dbar E^0(X) (Theorems 8.1-8.9)
Ch. 8 Theorem 8.10 and Corollary 8.11, printed pp. 81–82, for scalar structure-sheaf duality; Ch. 11 “Pairings,” printed pp. 95–96, for the divisor product and residue functional
contents.proof_mapping: The scalar case and product convention corroborate notation; the proof here uses the line-bundle harmonic-star route provisionally. McMullen’s later dimension-count completion is not used.

contents.name: Ch. 9: divisors, principal divisors, the degree homomorphism and deg(f)=0
Ch. 9: the sheaves O_D, the isomorphism O_D=O_{D+(f)}, and the space of constrained forms Omega_D
Ch. 9, equation (9.1), Theorems 9.2-9.4, printed pp. 85-86: the skyscraper sequence, alternating dimensions, and higher-cohomology vanishing.
contents.proof_mapping: Corroborates the exact-sequence route. Its phrase “polar part” is interpreted as the Laurent coefficient c_{-D(P)-1}; for negative D(P) this can be a Taylor coefficient, as the item states explicitly.

contents.name: Ch. 9: Riemann-Roch in Euler-characteristic form, chi(O_D)=chi(O)+deg D, with chi(O)=1-ga (Theorem 9.1)
contents.proof_mapping: Theorem 9.1 and its proof give chi(O_D)=chi(O)+deg D by the skyscraper exact sequence. The printed proof uses the arithmetic genus g_a=dim Omega(X) and explicitly says g_a=g will be shown later; A10 supplies that identification here. Focused local scope repair: intrinsic RR at D=−(g+2)[p] yields a nonzero section of K_X tensor O((g+2)[p]); division by the canonical meromorphic divisor-bundle section proves existence of a nonzero meromorphic differential and restores the unconditional canonical-divisor formula. This added argument is local supplier reasoning, not a new source-reading claim.

contents.name: Ch. 9: existence of a nonconstant map to P^1 of degree at most ga+1; canonical divisors exist and the arithmetic and topological genus agree (Theorems 9.6-9.11)
contents.proof_mapping: Theorem 9.6 proves existence with bound g_a+1; its proof uses Riemann-Roch, and Corollary 9.11 later identifies g_a with topological genus. This item cites the theorem as corroboration; A10 supplies the topological-genus convention, while the proof uses A15 and handles genus zero separately. RR now supplies nonzero meromorphic-differential existence unconditionally; the canonical correction vanishes at every genus because deg(K−2g[p])=−2, with the genus-zero nonconstant function still obtained from [p].

contents.name: Ch. 12: maps to projective space defined by linear systems, separation of points and tangents, and the Veronese examples
Ch. 14: holomorphic line bundles, frames, cocycles and the associated line bundle of a divisor
Ch. 9, printed p. 85: the interpretation h^0(nP)=1,1,2,3,... on a torus
contents.proof_mapping: Forster Exercises 16.1–16.2 (printed p. 131) and McMullen Ch. 9 (printed p. 85) were read in the full PDFs. Verification steps 1.1–3.1 prove the sphere dimensions and canonical divisor with H^0(K)=0, torus genus and dimensions, and the explicit Weierstrass distinct-pole-order basis; no Leray-cover claim is imported.

contents.name: Ch. 12: the rational normal curve as the image of the linear system d*infinity on P^1
Ch. 12, printed pp. 103–104: Theorem 12.2, the map from a base-point-free linear system to projective space and its basis-coordinate formula
Ch. 14, Theorem 14.2, printed p. 119: finite-dimensionality of H^1(X,L) for an arbitrary line bundle; the text refers to Forster, Ch. 29, for the proof.
contents.proof_mapping: Corroborates the general line-bundle statement, but the cited passage is only a theorem assertion; this item uses the Hodge supplier and Demailly’s complete elliptic/Hodge argument instead.

contents.name: Ch. 8 Theorem 8.10, printed pp. 81–82, and Ch. 9 Theorems 9.1 and 9.5, printed pp. 85–87: the structure-sheaf cohomology, χ(O)=1−g_a and finite-dimensionality
contents.proof_mapping: Alternative structure-sheaf calculation. McMullen uses arithmetic genus g_a and proves g_a=g later by Riemann–Roch; this item derives the topological genus relation without using a later Riemann–Roch result.

contents.name: Ch. 11, “Pairings,” printed pp. 95–96: the product O₋D⊗ΩD→Ω, the residue trace on H¹(X,Ω), and the functional φ(ξ)=Res(ξω)
Ch. 11 §§11.1 and “Pairings”, printed pp. 94–97: the canonical Serre-duality statement and residue functional from O_{−D}⊗Ω_D→Ω.
contents.proof_mapping: McMullen’s dimension-count arguments are not imported; A12 supplies the preceding Hodge-star proof used by this item.

contents.name: Ch. 10, “Mittag–Leffler problems,” Theorem 10.5, printed pp. 89–92; Ch. 11, Theorem 11.1 and “Pairings,” printed pp. 94–96.
contents.proof_mapping: Theorem 10.5 states the function-valued residue criterion using Serre duality. This item rederives it from A13; the scaffold’s Ch. 9 pp. 86–88 locator was unrelated.

sources.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007 author lecture notes)

contents.name: Ch. 3 §4 Corollary 3.32: the Hodge-Weyl decomposition and dim Omega(S)=g
contents.proof_mapping: Alternate Hodge–Weyl route to dim H^0(K)=g. This item derives the same dimension from the holomorphic de Rham exact sequence and harmonic-star duality; the Hodge–Weyl statement is not used as a proof input.

contents.name: Ch. 4 §1-3: divisors, orders, principal and canonical divisors, degree and linear equivalence
Ch. 5 §§1-2: the map defined by a linear system and the embedding criterion (Proposition 5.7)
Ch. 6 §1, Proposition 6.1, printed pp. 53-54: the nested-divisor principal-part exact sequence and local quotient dimension deg(D)-deg(D').
contents.proof_mapping: Read as an alternative principal-parts model. The item proves the sheaf sequence directly by stalks and does not identify Looijenga’s cokernel notation with the sheaf-cohomology group without an additional theorem.

contents.name: Ch. 6 §2, Definition 6.2 and Proposition 6.3, printed pp. 54–55: the local residue integral, finite residue support on compact X, and the Stokes orientation in the residue theorem
Ch. 6 §3 Corollary 6.6: dim L(D)-dim H^1(D)=1-g+deg D and deg K=2g-2
contents.proof_mapping: Proposition 6.1 and Corollary 6.6 were read through their proofs. They give the divisor exact sequence and Riemann-Roch formula; the proof also establishes existence of a nonconstant meromorphic map and computes deg K by Riemann-Hurwitz. This item instead uses A9, A10 and A13, and does not import that route. Focused local scope repair: intrinsic RR at D=−(g+2)[p] yields a nonzero section of K_X tensor O((g+2)[p]); division by the canonical meromorphic divisor-bundle section proves existence of a nonzero meromorphic differential and restores the unconditional canonical-divisor formula. This added argument is local supplier reasoning, not a new source-reading claim.

contents.name: Ch. 6 §4, Theorem 6.7 and proof, printed pp. 56–57: the residue map from differentials constrained by D to H¹(D)*.
contents.proof_mapping: The source’s injectivity construction and statement corroborate the residue pairing; its surjectivity proof uses Riemann–Roch and is not imported.

contents.name: Ch. 6 Exercise 6.1: residues of d(log phi) and the degree-zero obstruction for principal divisors
Ch. 2: the topological classification of compact surfaces and the genus
Ch. 5 §1, printed pp. 48–51: Proposition 5.6, the holomorphic map from a linear system without fixed points to its dual projective space
Ch. 6 §1, Proposition 6.1, printed pp. 53-54, and §3, Corollary 6.6, printed p. 55: the divisor principal-part model and finite-dimensionality in Riemann-Roch.
contents.proof_mapping: Read as an alternative divisor-theoretic literature argument. It is not used as an earlier library dependency; the item proof uses the Hodge finiteness chain.

contents.name: Ch. 6 §4, Theorem 6.7, printed pp. 56–57: the classical residue-duality statement
contents.proof_mapping: Its proof uses Riemann–Roch, so it is recorded only as the classical shape of the result and is not used to justify this earlier proof.

contents.name: Ch. 6 §2, Proposition 6.3 and Theorem 6.4, printed pp. 54–55: global residue theorem and the converse residue theorem for differentials.
contents.proof_mapping: Proposition 6.3 supplies the necessary residue theorem; Theorem 6.4 concerns meromorphic differentials, while the function-valued sufficiency argument is proved locally here using A13.

contents.name: Ch. 6 §3, Corollary 6.6 and proof: Riemann-Roch and deg K=2g−2
contents.proof_mapping: The proof establishes the RR formula and degree of K by constructing a nonconstant meromorphic map and applying Riemann-Hurwitz. This item derives deg K at every genus from A10/A13/A15 instead and keeps the upstream Hodge-dependent suppliers open. RR now supplies nonzero meromorphic-differential existence unconditionally; the canonical correction vanishes at every genus because deg(K−2g[p])=−2, with the genus-zero nonconstant function still obtained from [p].

sources.title: Anand Deopurkar, Riemann-Roch (MATH 8320/2017 algebraic curves course notes, University of California Davis)

contents.name: §2.1: the Riemann-Roch and Serre duality statements (1)-(3) for a divisor D on a compact Riemann surface, including the perfect pairing given by summation of residues
contents.proof_mapping: Theorem 2.1 and Lemma 2.2 state the Euler formula and point-divisor increment; §2.1 derives the former by finite induction. The note establishes finiteness using its unproved Theorem 1.1 on ample divisors/Serre vanishing, and its duality proof is in §§2.2–2.3. This item uses the assigned A8–A13 chain instead. Focused local scope repair: intrinsic RR at D=−(g+2)[p] yields a nonzero section of K_X tensor O((g+2)[p]); division by the canonical meromorphic divisor-bundle section proves existence of a nonzero meromorphic differential and restores the unconditional canonical-divisor formula. This added argument is local supplier reasoning, not a new source-reading claim.

contents.name: §§2.1–2.3, printed pp. 2–5: perfect residue-pairing statement, injectivity construction and surjectivity proof.
contents.proof_mapping: The surjectivity argument uses Serre vanishing via an ample divisor; this item uses A12’s Hodge-star proof and treats Deopurkar as independent corroboration.

contents.name: §2.4, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 6): residue-pairing interpretation of the function-valued criterion and worked examples.
contents.proof_mapping: Independent corroboration; the notes invoke Serre duality, while this proof uses A13 provisionally.

contents.name: Lemma 19.5.1: enough injectives for sheaves of modules on a ringed space
contents.proof_mapping: Supports the supplied module-injective resolution in step 2.1.

contents.name: Lemma 20.8.1: injective module sheaves are flasque
contents.proof_mapping: Supports the flasqueness of each module-injective resolution term; the library also supplies the derived-cohomology acyclicity theorem.

sources.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry (author manuscript, Universite Grenoble Alpes)

contents.name: Ch. VI §2, (2.1)-(2.8), printed pp. 288-290, and §7, (7.1)-(7.2), printed pp. 309-310: elliptic finiteness and closed range, Hodge decomposition, and finite-dimensional Dolbeault cohomology for a holomorphic Hermitian bundle on a compact Hermitian manifold.
contents.proof_mapping: The item applies the line-bundle Hodge finiteness statement through the Hodge supplier. Demailly §7 states the arbitrary holomorphic Hermitian bundle result; §2 supplies the compact elliptic kernel and closed-range argument. The independent library proof chain is still open at the in-run Hodge corollary.

contents.name: Ch. VI §7, (7.1)–(7.4), printed pp. 309–310: finite-dimensional Dolbeault cohomology and Serre duality, with the pairing factoring through cohomology and nondegeneracy following from the positive Hodge-star norm
contents.proof_mapping: Supports the exact Hodge finiteness and duality input used provisionally in step 4.1. The matching batch-9 item files are unfinished, so this source corroborates but does not discharge those library-supplier obligations.

contents.name: Ch. VI §7, (7.3)–(7.4), printed p. 310: line-bundle-valued Serre pairing, Stokes factorization, harmonic-star correspondence, and positivity of the norm
contents.proof_mapping: The item checks the one-dimensional line-bundle case through harmonic representatives and the nonzero scalar factor in A11; the corresponding in-run Hodge suppliers are still missing.

contents.name: Ch. VI §7, (7.3)–(7.4), printed p. 310: the Dolbeault Serre pairing, its Stokes factorization and harmonic-star identification.
contents.proof_mapping: This is the analytic argument behind the provisional Hodge-star supplier used by A12 and by step 4.1; the in-run supplier file remains missing.
